name: Bright Angel
convention: East-positive longitude from -180 to 180 and planetocentric latitude, in degrees. Heights in metres relative to the areoid.

grid.rowOrder: north row first; within a row, west cell first

files.name: heightM
files.meaning: Mean terrain height of the 4 x 4 source cells in the routing cell, relative to the areoid.

files.name: slopeMaxDeg
files.meaning: Steepest slope found among the 4 x 4 source cells in the routing cell. Each source cell's slope is measured over 6.0 m north to south and 5.69 m east to west. Use it for keep-out; for effort use the slope along the direction of travel, taken from heightM.

home.name: Crew rover
home.why: Assumed for this scenario: the crew's pressurised rover parks where Perseverance itself stood for 16 sols (sol 1068 to 1083), on ground the rover's drivers chose and reached, with the rover tilted 8.5 degrees.
home.positionSource: Perseverance waypoints file, stop 50_1618, first logged on sol 1068

targets.name: Cheyava Falls
targets.why: The rock NASA described as having features that may bear on whether Mars was once home to microscopic life. Perseverance cored it on 21 July 2024 at the northern edge of Neretva Vallis.
targets.positionSource: Perseverance waypoints file, stop 56_0, first logged on sol 1210

targets.name: Rover stop 56_3438
targets.why: Perseverance stayed here 13 sols (sol 1231 to 1243), the second-longest stay in this box, so its team found enough here to stop and work.
targets.positionSource: Perseverance waypoints file, stop 56_3438, first logged on sol 1231

targets.name: Rover stop 59_204
targets.why: Perseverance stayed here 10 sols (sol 1254 to 1263) on its climb out of the valley, about 108 m above the crew rover. The hardest walk of the three.
targets.positionSource: Perseverance waypoints file, stop 59_204, first logged on sol 1254

readFrom.terrain: local working copy, first read from the team data server
